item.title: CT small businesses hope their latest R&D tax credit push pays off
item.description: Lawmakers are again considering expanding the state’s R&D tax credit to small businesses. Advocates are hopeful it will pass this session.

item.title: My school is grading me with AI. It got my grade wrong.
item.description: AI produces errors serious enough to require a dispute button built right into the tool. So how many students, facing an error, simply accept the score and move on.

item.title: Blue states push to ban ICE at polls amid federal voter intimidation fears
item.description: Several Democratic states—including CT—are moving to bar federal immigration agents from being near polling places and other election sites.

item.title: CT state police deploy new multimillion-dollar technology, equipment
item.description: Troopers demonstrated new tasers, bodycams, virtual reality training and other software Wednesday. CT has approved $120M for the equipment.

item.title: CT lawmakers consider new regulations on wake surfing
item.description: The proposal would allow wake surfing to take place within 200 feet of the shoreline on most Connecticut lakes, with some exceptions.

item.title: CT senators respond to Kristi Noem firing: ‘She was horrible’
item.description: Richard Blumenthal and Chris Murphy said even with Noem gone, Homeland Security needs to undertake a vastly different approach.

item.title: CT, 23 other states sue Trump over new tariffs after SCOTUS loss
item.description: More states have joined CT in a lawsuit against the Trump administration’s new tariffs after the Supreme Court's ruling on the previous ones.

item.title: Lawmakers advance nominations of new PURA board
item.description: Lamont's four PURA nominees cleared a legislative hurdle after hours of questioning over what they might do about CT's high electricity costs.

item.title: Sen. Ceci Maher to retire, says it is time for next generation
item.description: Sen. Ceci Maher, 72, announced she will not seek reelection, but will instead step aside so "younger leaders" can take the reins.

item.title: Beware unintended consequences of CT social media legislation
item.description: CT children face real risks online, and doing nothing isn't acceptable. But HB5037 doesn't give parents the tools they're asking for.
